outcome: Mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal, instrumental vaginal, cesarean)
cohort: The study included 211 women with term, singleton pregnancies delivering large-for-gestational-age fetuses (birthweight >= 90th percentile), excluding those with prior cesarean, multiples, preterm birth, non-cephalic presentation, planned cesarean, maternal request, or incomplete records.
finding: Nulliparity, induction of labor, greater gestational weight gain, and prenatal suspicion of macrosomia were independently associated with an increased risk of non-spontaneous birth in LGA pregnancies.
mod_finding: In LGA pregnancies, nulliparity and suspected macrosomia were associated with higher rates of medical intervention (operative delivery), while induction of labor and prior vaginal delivery favored spontaneous birth.
